While serving on the Brighton Town Board, I championed gender‑neutral language, founded the IDEA Committee to amplify diverse voices, revived our environmental and beautification efforts, and pushed for safer traffic routes and bike lanes—each action rooted in the belief that every resident deserves a voice and a thriving community. I also secured a Community Choice Aggregation program that will lower energy costs and power our town with 100% renewable energy. My parents, immigrants from Guyana who worked as healthcare professionals, showed me the power of opportunity and hard work, shaping my commitment to the American Dream for all. Today, I ask for your support in Congress so we can expand that dream—ensuring transparent governance, protecting our environment, and guaranteeing that every New Yorker in the 25th District can access the economic and educational opportunities that made my family’s story possible. Together, we will build a future where equity, justice, and opportunity are not privileges but rights for everyone.

Friends, neighbors, and fellow citizens of New York’s 25th District, I’m Robin Wilt, a lifelong Rochester resident who has called Brighton home with my husband Nick and our three sons since 2003, and I am running for Congress to make sure that every child who walks the streets of this community—and every family in our state—has the same opportunity to live the American Dream that my parents, first‑generation immigrants from Guyana, earned through hard work, education, and hope. As a real‑estate professional and former Brighton Town Board member, I have turned grassroots advocacy into concrete results: we adopted gender‑neutral language in all town communications, created the IDEA Committee to champion inclusion for our growing diversity, re‑established an Environmental and Beautification Committee that fuels recycling and community pride, and championed bike lanes and smarter traffic routing in partnership with the state DOT—all while pushing for Community Choice Aggregation to lower energy costs and secure 100 % renewable sourcing for our residents. My record shows that transparent governance and active civic participation can translate into real policy that protects our schools, our environment, and our families. I will bring the same dedication, equity‑first mindset, and relentless pursuit of social justice to Washington, D.C., ensuring that the promise of prosperity is not a privilege of a few but a right for all. Join me in building a future where every voice is heard, every dream is reachable, and every dollar spent in our district goes toward a stronger, more inclusive community. Vote for Robin Wilt for Congress.

Thompson is a small vineyard owner and was the maintenance supervisor for the Beringer Winery. He has taught Public Administration and State Government at San Francisco State University and California State University, Chico.

He is married to Janet Thompson, a family nurse practitioner. They have two sons, a firefighter and a deputy sheriff, and three wonderful granddaughters.

Lauren is a graduate of the University of Michigan and Johns Hopkins University.

Trent has worked at McRaes Department Store as a manager, maintained a private law practice in Saltillo, and served as Tupelo City Prosecutor and Forfeiture Attorney for North Mississippi Narcotics Unit. Prior to being elected to Congress, Trent served as a District Attorney for the 1st Circuit Judicial District (Lee, Pontotoc, Alcorn, Monroe, Itawamba, Prentiss, and Tishomingo) managing all felony cases.

In Congress, Trent serves on the House Armed Services Committee, serving as the Ranking Member of the Military Personnel Subcommittee.  Trent also serves on the House Agriculture Committee.

Following the example of my father, I promised myself that I would dedicate the rest of my life to being a voice for those that never get a seat at the table.
